bodies.intuition: Attention heads each keep their own keys and values, and at generation time all of them sit in memory. Multi-query attention keeps the separate queries but shares one set of keys and values across every head, shrinking the cache by the number of heads at a small cost in quality.
bodies.engineer: Project queries per head as usual; project a single K and V shared by all heads. The cache shrinks by a factor of h, which is what makes long contexts affordable at generation time. Training from scratch with it loses a little quality, and models converted after the fact need a short adaptation phase.
bodies.math: head_i = Attention(XW_Q^i, XW_K, XW_V) with W_K and W_V shared. Cache size falls from 2·h·d_head·n to 2·d_head·n per layer. Arithmetic intensity rises correspondingly, which is why the gain at generation time is larger than the parameter saving suggests.

emphasis.intuition: shrinking the cache by the number of heads
